title: Alcohols, Phenols & Ethers
subject: Chemistry
tagline: From hand sanitiser to aspirin to the first surgical anaesthetic — one oxygen atom, three personalities. Every JEE Main idea on alcohols, phenols and ethers, with labs you can play with.

lessons.title: Meet the –OH Family
lessons.summary: One oxygen atom, three personalities. Learn to classify, name and picture alcohols, phenols and ethers — and why none of their bond angles is the textbook 109.5°.

lessons.title: Making Alcohols
lessons.summary: Three roads to an –OH: add water across a C=C (two ways, opposite answers), reduce a C=O, or let a Grignard reagent build the carbon skeleton for you.

lessons.title: Making Phenols
lessons.summary: A 300-atmosphere pressure cooker, a salt that fizzes nitrogen, and the cumene process that makes phenol and acetone in one go.

lessons.title: Boiling Points & Solubility
lessons.summary: Why ethanol boils almost 100 K above an ether of the same mass, why ethanol mixes with water but butanol barely does — and why one nitrophenol escapes with steam.

lessons.title: Acidity: Who Lets Go of H⁺?
lessons.summary: Sodium fizzes with all of them, but only phenol dissolves in caustic soda. The whole story is the stability of the anion left behind — and you can watch it on the pKa ladder.

lessons.title: Breaking C–O: Substitution & Dehydration
lessons.summary: Turn –OH into a leaving group and alcohols become halides, alkenes or ethers. Race the Lucas test, and step through the carbocation that sometimes rearranges itself.

lessons.title: Oxidation & Telling Alcohols Apart
lessons.summary: Primary, secondary or tertiary? Oxidise it, heat it on copper, or look for a yellow iodoform cloud. Plus the chemistry inside a police breathalyser.

lessons.title: Phenol’s Hyperactive Ring
lessons.summary: The –OH makes the benzene ring so electron-rich that bromine water alone puts on three bromines. Nitration, halogenation, Kolbe, Reimer–Tiemann — all in one explorer.

lessons.title: Ethers: The Quiet Cousins
lessons.summary: Unreactive enough to be the perfect solvent, until HI arrives. Williamson synthesis, its one big trap, and which side of the oxygen the iodide attacks.

lessons.title: Wrap-up: The Reaction Map
lessons.summary: Every reaction of the chapter on one map, a detective case with four bottles of C₄H₁₀O, and Reagent Rush — a quick-fire game to lock it all in.
